campaign: Student movement and end of one-party rule
observed_result: Student-led pluralism demands became part of a multi-stage transition ending communist one-party government; opposition won the 1992 election.
long_term_caution: Regime transformation unfolded across negotiations; mobilization; strikes; and elections, not a single protest victory.
comparison_question: Why did student mobilization accompany foundational change in 1990 but only policy responses in 2018?

observed_result: Pyramid-scheme failures triggered riots; armed unrest; a collapse of state control and a change of government after elections.
long_term_caution: Not a straightforward civil-resistance campaign: state breakdown and widespread armed violence preclude treating it as nonviolent success.
comparison_question: Why does state collapse differ analytically from nonviolent regime transition?

observed_result: Government announced tuition and university-policy measures responding to student demands.
long_term_caution: A later qualitative study finds limited durable institutional change; promises and implementation must be assessed separately.
comparison_question: Can concessions address immediate demands without solving underlying institutional grievances?

observed_result: As of 18 October 2026, reporting describes a sixth consecutive day of student and broader anti-government demonstrations in Tirana, further police-protester clashes, and Prime Minister Edi Rama declining calls to resign. No final campaign result is established.
long_term_caution: A dated news snapshot, not an outcome forecast. Reported violent incidents do not characterize all participants; claims about violence and policing require source-specific attribution and independent review.
comparison_question: How do changing demands and escalating confrontations affect a movement whose political outcome is still unresolved?

observed_result: Post-election mobilization helped force recognition of opposition victory and the departure of Slobodan Milosevic.
long_term_caution: Elections; opposition coalition-building; strikes and security-force behavior all contributed. Do not claim street protests acted alone.
comparison_question: How did an electoral dispute interact with organization and state noncooperation?

observed_result: Serzh Sargsyan resigned as prime minister after mass protests; subsequent parliamentary processes installed a new government.
long_term_caution: Leadership removal and later institutional reforms are different outcomes; the label captures the immediate milestone only.
comparison_question: What was the role of parliamentary politics after the resignation?

campaign: Revolution and end of Ben Ali rule
observed_result: Ben Ali was removed and a multiparty democratic opening followed.
long_term_caution: Democratic gains later reversed as the presidency consolidated authority from 2021; immediate and durable outcomes diverge.
comparison_question: Why did the initial democratic opening not guarantee long-term democratic resilience?

observed_result: Mubarak resigned and the military initially assumed direct authority; later elections were followed by a 2013 military takeover.
long_term_caution: Do not confuse removing the president with dismantling the military's power within the state.
comparison_question: Which institutions outlasted leadership change and shaped the subsequent reversal?

observed_result: Large protests following the disputed election did not remove Lukashenko; mass arrests and repression followed.
long_term_caution: Campaign endpoint is simplified to the 2020–2021 protest wave, not the end of all Belarusian opposition activity.
comparison_question: Why did mass participation coexist with continued incumbent control?

observed_result: President Gotabaya Rajapaksa resigned following mass protests; parliament selected a successor.
long_term_caution: Subsequent political changes cannot all be attributed to the movement. Some protest episodes involved property damage and violent confrontations.
comparison_question: Why did a leadership exit leave the constitutional system largely intact?

observed_result: Authorities withdrew the extradition bill; several wider political demands remained unmet.
long_term_caution: A partial demand met does not mean that the movement's broader aims succeeded; restrictions on civil society later intensified.
comparison_question: When is one substantial policy concession a partial success rather than general movement success?

observed_result: Student-led mobilization widened after repression; Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled in August 2024.
long_term_caution: The UN documented serious repression and subsequent retaliatory violence; the durability and direction of political change must be evaluated separately.
comparison_question: How do student grievances become nationwide demands for political change, and at what cost?
